name: RUSSELN
description: Russeln (Ramscheln/Ramsch variant) is a German Rams-family game for 3-5 players. 32-card German pack. Dealer antes; 5 each; widow. Bid: play, pass, or ramsch (take all 5 tricks). Follow suit; trump; head trick. 1/5 pot per trick. Successful ramsch wins pot + 5 from each. Players may drop if they expect to fail.

content.text: Russeln (Ramscheln/Ramsch variant) is a German Rams-family game for 3-5 players. 32-card German pack. Dealer antes; 5 each; widow. Bid: play, pass, or ramsch (take all 5 tricks). Follow suit; trump; head trick. 1/5 pot per trick. Successful ramsch wins pot + 5 from each. Players may drop if they expect to fail.

Russeln (Ramscheln) is the modern German variety of the Rams family. Rams is a European trick-taking game related to Nap and Loo; in Germany it appears as Rams, Rammes, Ramsch, Ramschen or Ramscheln. Parlett describes the family as a nineteenth-century French, Alsatian and Belgian pastime and a loose-knit group of gambling and drinking games. Rules were first published in France around 1820; Austrian sources banned Ramschen as early as 1826, and a Bavarian account describes the rural game of Ramsen around 1800. The 1862 Freiberger Biercomment codified Rammes with a widow and the 7 of Bells as second-highest trump; the American game Rounce (1868) was derived from German Ramsch and played with a 32-card pack. Ramscheln remains the authentic modern German equivalent, typically played with a 32-card German pack, five cards each, and a widow.
32-card German pack (four suits: Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells; ranks 7 through Ace). Five cards each plus a widow; dealer antes 5.
